name: Simultaneous Extensions Retaining a Negative Reduction Are Forbidden
statement: Let $X\subseteq Y\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, with $X$ an irredundant forbidden pc-minor. If an active coordinate $e$ satisfies $X^{\{e\}}=Y^{\{e\}}\notin\mathsf{Damp}$ and $Y$ peels to $X$, then $Y$ is a forbidden pc-minor. It is enough that every connected component of $G(Y\setminus X)$ be a tree or have at most eight vertices; the number of components and the sizes of tree components are unrestricted, and no addition order or proper-minor peeling certificates need be supplied.
proof: Apply any elementary old-coordinate operation $\mu$ to the relative deletion sequence from $Y$ to $X$ and omit repeated images. The remaining singleton changes form a relative peeling from $\mu Y$ to the positive proper minor $\mu X$, so every proper elementary minor of $Y$ is dismantlable ample. The shared negative reduction keeps $Y$ outside that class, proving forbiddenness. Under the graph condition, component expansion makes $X\cup K$ ample for each residual component $K$; the relative forest theorem or the theorem through eight relative facets peels it to $X$. Components are mutually nonadjacent, so their orders concatenate and the first part applies.
comments: No converse is claimed: an arbitrary reduction-preserving extension need not have these component graphs, and a reduced obstruction need not contain a suitable smaller forbidden input.
